text.p: Lithuania's fridge producer Snaige said on Tuesday that its net profit in April was 60,000 litas compared to losses of 100,000 litas in the same month last year.
The company's president, Antanas Andrulionis, also told Reuters that sales in April reached 11 million litas.
The company earlier reported a first quarter loss of 4.2 million litas and sales of 22 million litas.
Its net profit for all of 1996 was 624,870 litas on sales of 145.26 million litas.
"We expect our sales to grow around 20 percent in May and in June we will have difficulty meetings all of the new orders for our fridges," Andrulionis said.
Andrulionis also said that the main task for the company is to compensate for the losses of the first three months of the year.
"After we have made up for the losses we intend to call a general shareholders' meeting to decide on a share capital increase from additional contributions," Andrulionis said.
"It could happen in autumn," he added.
The company said earlier that it was mulling a share capital boost of 40 million litas to 60 million litas this year and that it was in talks with foreign investors.

Snaige, located in the southern Lithuanian city of Alytus, is listed on the A group of the Vilnius bourse. The company's shares rose by 29.4 percent to 11 litas last week and continued to gain on Monday.
The price rise was fueled by rumours that Estonia's Hansa Bank had acquired a five percent stake in the company last week, dealers said.
